name: The War Loan
about: One great house paid for the crown's last war, and now it wants a say in the next one: where the host marches, and against whom. Pay it back, give it a seat at the war council, or refuse, and face the sellswords its silver hires and the claim it backs.
title: The War Loan

beats.speaker: rich
beats.text: {rich}'s steward rides in from {bank} with the old King's seal on a note: the silver {rich.house} lent for the last war, and the interest. {rich} doesn't want it all back. {rich.He} wants a say in where the host marches next.

court.text: {rich} of {rich.house}: "My silver paid for your father's spears, Your Grace. Give me a voice in your war council, or give me my silver."

options.label: Pay the first part from the treasury (500 gold)
options.hint: {rich.houseName} is owed less · the war chest is empty
options.result: The crown pays. {rich}'s steward counts it twice and says he'll be back in a year for the rest.

options.label: Give {rich} a seat at the war council
options.hint: {rich.houseName} +15 · {poor.houseName} −10, who sees a lender steering the King's host · {rich.house} lends 200 gold for the next campaign
options.result: {rich} takes a chair at the war table, and {rich.his} steward leaves a chest of silver for the next campaign. Every other lord at court counts the chairs and sees whose is new.

options.label: Refuse: the crown doesn't pay its father's debts
options.hint: nothing now · {rich.houseName} has other ways to collect
options.result: The King tears the note in half. The steward picks up both halves and rides home to {bank}.

beats.speaker: rich
beats.text: {rich} names the price of the rest of the debt: the royal host is to march against {poor.house}, whose lands lie across {rich.house}'s trade roads.

court.text: {poor} of {poor.house}: "{rich} wants your host at my gates to settle a quarrel over tolls, Your Grace. Do it, and every house learns the King's spears are for hire."

options.label: Pay off the rest from the treasury (600 gold)
options.hint: the debt is done · {poor.houseName} +10 · the crown is poor
options.result: The crown pays the last of it. {rich} has nothing left to ask for, and {poor} rides home grateful.

options.label: Let {rich.house} make its own war on {poor.house}
options.hint: {rich.houseName} +10 · {poor.houseName} −30 · two houses at war, and the King stands aside
options.result: The King tells {rich} the debt is forgiven if {rich.he} fights {rich.his} own quarrel. {rich.house}'s host is on the road to {poor.house} within the month.

options.label: Refuse: the King's host is not for hire
options.result: The King refuses. {poor} thanks him in open court. {rich} doesn't argue, and leaves early.

beats.speaker: rich
beats.text: What the crown won't pay, {rich} collects another way. {rich.house}'s silver has hired a sellsword company, and it has spent the winter at {bank}.

court.text: {poor}: "Five thousand sellswords at {bank}, Your Grace, paid with the interest on your father's war. Buy them, or they'll come for the debt with a different King."

options.label: Outbid {rich} for the sellswords (700 gold)
options.hint: the company changes sides: three companies of knights for the King · the debt is still owed
options.result: The crown pays more than {rich}. The sellsword captain kneels to the King, for a year.

options.label: Take {bank} from {rich} and give it to {poor.house}
options.result: By royal decree, {bank} goes to {poor.house} to hold for the King. {rich} doesn't open the gates.

beats.speaker: rich
beats.text: With {rich.his} silver and {rich.his} sellswords, {rich} says a King who can't pay for his wars can't keep his throne. {rich.house} calls its banners and marches.

beats.speaker: poor
beats.text: The war loan is settled, one way or another. {rich.house} has its silver or its seat, and the other houses know exactly what it cost.

beats.speaker: poor
beats.text: {rich}'s host is broken outside Kingsmere. The crown never pays, and no house lends the King silver for a war again.
